entities.summary: Katyn war cemetery is a Polish military cemetery located in Katyn, a small village 22 kilometres away from Smolensk, Russia, on the road to Vitebsk. It contains the remnants of 4,412 Polish officers of the Kozelsk prisoner of war camp, who were murdered in 1940 in what is called the Katyn massacre. Except for bodies of two Polish generals exhumed by German authorities in 1943 and then buried separately, all Polish officers murdered in Katyn were buried in six large mass graves. There is also a Russian part of the cemetery, where some 6,500 victims of the Soviet Great Purges of the 1930s were buried by the NKVD.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Katyn massacre resulted in the murder of 4,412 Polish officers and had significant regional impact on Poland's relations with the Soviet Union. The discovery of mass graves at the site led to a reevaluation of Soviet involvement in the event.
